userStories.title: Canonical tools[] ordering at wire-time + literal tool_call preservation
userStories.description: Land the byte-faithfulness substrate that A03 depends on. Two distinct fixes bundled because they share the same wire-layer ownership: (a) CANONICAL TOOLS[] ORDERING — in internal/llm/client.go (or wherever the request payload is built), sort the `tools` array LEXICOGRAPHICALLY BY NAME at marshal-time, regardless of registry insertion order. This guards against MCP reconciler ([[project_wave_2_10_b_tool_reconciler_shipped]]) reordering the registry mid-session and silently breaking cache. Implementation: just before json.Marshal, do `sort.Slice(req.Tools, func(i,j int){ return req.Tools[i].Name < req.Tools[j].Name })`. Idempotent. Determinism is the goal — same registry contents → same byte output. (b) LITERAL TOOL_CALL PRESERVATION — if A01 found Aura re-serializes tool_call responses (the JSON-shaped output that the model produced when calling a tool), refactor the archive + replay path to preserve LITERAL BYTES. This means: when the model responds with `tool_calls: [...]`, capture the raw JSON sub-tree as bytes (not re-marshaled struct), and on subsequent turns inject those bytes verbatim into the next request. Storage shape: a new `tool_calls_raw BLOB` column on conversations table (migration v25) holding the byte slice; the existing `tool_calls_json TEXT` stays for human-readable archive. Reader prefers `tool_calls_raw` if present, falls back to `tool_calls_json` for legacy rows. (c) TESTS — internal/llm/client_test.go gains TestRequest_ToolsSortedLexico (100 random-shuffle inputs produce same JSON output) + TestRequest_StableAcrossRuns (build the same request twice from same inputs, assert byte-identical output). internal/conversation/archive_test.go gains TestArchive_ToolCallLiteralBytesRoundTrip (write bytes → read back → bit-identical). (d) IF A01 returned 'Aura is already byte-faithful' verdict, this story collapses to JUST the canonical ordering work. The literal-bytes preservation becomes an optional reinforcement that the story can include or defer to a follow-up.

userStories.title: Per-provider capability flag + cache_control marker injection
userStories.description: Wire prompt-cache markers into the LLM client, gated by per-provider capability. Pattern lifted from D:/tmp/nanobot (docs/kv-cache-research/local-implementations-2026-05-20.md). (a) PROVIDER CAPABILITY MATRIX — new file internal/llm/cache_capability.go (~80 LOC) defining `type CacheCapability struct { ProviderID string; SupportsCacheControl bool; MarkerStyle string; LookbackBlocks int }` and a default registry: anthropic={true, anthropic_ephemeral, 20}, openai={true, openai_auto, 0/* automatic */}, gemini={true, gemini_context_cache, 0}, mistral={false, '', 0}, llama_server={false, '', 0}, default={false, '', 0}. ProviderID detection: from explicit `LLM_PROVIDER` env (preferred) or heuristic on base_url hostname (`api.anthropic.com` → anthropic, `api.openai.com` → openai, etc.). Default OFF if unknown — sending unknown JSON keys to a strict provider returns HTTP 400 (nanobot test #167-178). (b) MARKER INJECTION — in internal/llm/client.go marshal path, when capability.SupportsCacheControl + MarkerStyle=='anthropic_ephemeral': inject `{ "type": "text", "text": "...", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"} }` at THREE breakpoints: (i) END of system-prompt block (system+tool-definitions are the longest-stable prefix), (ii) at the MCP/builtin tool BOUNDARY if Aura distinguishes them (so MCP churn invalidates only the tail, not the builtin head), (iii) ROLLING TAIL ANCHOR on the LAST user-message-or-tool-result block of the current turn. The rolling tail addresses Anthropic's 20-content-block lookback limit — without it, an 8-step agent loop with multiple tool_results per step silently falls out of cache (docs/kv-cache-research/providers-state-2026-05-20.md). (c) FOR openai_auto STYLE: no markers injected, but ensure request shape eligibility (≥1024 tokens, identical prefix across calls). (d) FOR gemini_context_cache STYLE: stub-only in this story — Gemini's API requires an explicit cache-create call upstream of message send, which is a larger refactor. Defer the wiring to a follow-up story; capability flag stays declared. (e) CONFIG WIRING — new env `AURA_LLM_CACHE_ENABLED` (default 'auto' → derive from capability matrix; 'off' → force disable; 'on' → force enable WITH WARNING in logs that this can 400 on strict providers). (f) TESTS — internal/llm/cache_capability_test.go covers the matrix + heuristic detection. internal/llm/client_test.go gains TestRequest_AnthropicCacheMarkers (verifies the 3 breakpoints are placed correctly given a multi-turn conversation), TestRequest_MistralNoCacheMarkers (verifies markers absent for strict provider), TestRequest_RollingTailMovesPerTurn (the tail anchor moves with the last block, not stuck on first turn).

(2) Read docs/kv-cache-research/local-implementations-2026-05-20.md for the nanobot helper shape — port to Go. (3) Read docs/kv-cache-research/providers-state-2026-05-20.md sections on Anthropic + OpenAI eligibility rules. (4) Read https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching for the LATEST 2026 marker format — there may have been a March 2026 TTL change. ROLLING TAIL DISCIPLINE: this is the subtle one. After each turn the agent loop appends tool_results + assistant message. The tail anchor must MOVE — last turn's anchor stays as a passive cache breakpoint, this turn's anchor goes on this turn's last block. Anthropic allows up to 4 cache_control breakpoints per request — so 3 breakpoints (system, MCP boundary, last turn tail) + 1 rolling anchor = exactly 4, fits the budget. If MCP boundary isn't applicable (no MCP tools loaded), drop to 3 active breakpoints. NEVER exceed 4 — Anthropic returns 400. STRICT-PROVIDER GUARD: nanobot's anti-pattern (test #167-178) is the strongest evidence — shipping cache_control to Mistral gives HTTP 400 on unknown keys. The capability gate MUST default to off-when-unknown. If a user sets AURA_LLM_CACHE_ENABLED=on while pointed at Mistral, the WARNING log on every request is the right tradeoff (don't silently swallow the user's override). PROBE TUNING: TestRequest_AnthropicCacheMarkers needs to construct a multi-turn fixture conversation and assert markers at the right indices. Pin the JSON shape so a future change to marker placement requires updating the test (regression guard). SCOPE DISCIPLINE: NO observability in this story — that's A04. NO probe binary — A05. The markers are a one-way send; the response-side cache hit metric belongs to A04. NO Gemini wiring beyond the capability declaration — Gemini's context cache requires an explicit create-cache API call that is a story-sized refactor on its own. userStories.title: 2-call probe + CI gate + 8-turn rolling-anchor validation
userStories.description: Close Phase-KV with a regression-proof probe binary + CI gate. (a) 2-CALL PROBE — new cmd/probe_kv_cache/main.go (~150 LOC). Mode 1 (default): two consecutive POSTs to Aura's chat endpoint with the SAME long-prefix conversation (fixture in cmd/probe_kv_cache/fixtures/long_prefix.json — a stable ~5 K-token conversation prompt that exercises tools). After call 2, query /api/health.kv_cache.hit_ratio_24h. Assert: `cache_read_input_tokens / prompt_tokens >= 0.7` on the second call (the threshold from docs/kv-cache-research/providers-state-2026-05-20.md). Pin the threshold in code as `const MinHitRatio = 0.70`. (b) 8-TURN ROLLING-ANCHOR TEST — Mode 2 (`-rolling`): 8 consecutive turns of an agent loop with multiple tool_results per turn. Assert that hit ratio STAYS above MinHitRatio across ALL 8 turns (not just turn 2). This validates the rolling tail anchor from A03 actually works — without it, the 20-content-block lookback kicks in around turn 4-5 and the test fails. Use a fixture conversation that deliberately accumulates ≥30 content blocks by turn 8. (c) PROVIDER-SKIP GATE — if /api/health reports provider not in {anthropic, openai-auto-eligible} or AURA_LLM_CACHE_ENABLED=off, the probe SKIPS (not FAILS) with a logged reason. Same pattern as cmd/probe_chat -tts gate. (d) CI INVOCATION — extend .github/workflows/ci.yml (or wherever CI lives) with opt-in step `if env.AURA_RUN_KV_PROBE == 'true'` that runs `go run ./cmd/probe_kv_cache -rolling`. Default OFF — runs only against live sidecars. (e) MAKEFILE TARGET — `kv-cache-probe` invokes the probe. (f) DOC — extend docs/tool-rag-eval-runbook.md (if it exists from Phase-RAG-A03) OR create docs/kv-cache-runbook.md with: when to run, how to interpret hit_ratio, what 'below threshold' means (cache not enabled vs threshold not met vs upstream broken vs byte-faithfulness regressed). (g) HEAD-OFF REGRESSION FIXTURE — add a `golden` JSON file that captures the EXACT request payload Aura sends for the rolling-anchor fixture.
